title: Data Augmentation of Contrastive Learning is Estimating Positive-incentive Noise
claim: A learned noise generator discovers meaningful, image-adaptive augmentations from raw inputs alone, without hand-designed transformations.
layout: 4 rows by 8 columns grid, top-to-bottom, row labels on left
description: A dense image grid with four labeled rows and eight columns of STL-10 examples (ship, airplane, eagle, car, dog with child, deer, cat, horse rider). Row 1, 'Original', shows the natural photographs. Row 2, 'Variance', shows jet-colormap heatmaps of the learned noise variance: objects and backgrounds light up in red or blue, depending on the image. Row 3, 'Noise', shows dark, speckled sampled noise with colored pixel grain and faint object silhouettes. Row 4, 'Augmentation', shows the original images with the noise added, giving color shifts, grain and stylized, style-transfer-like looks. Row labels are rotated text on the left. The eye goes first to the vivid heatmap row, then follows each column down from original to augmented.
caption: Visualization of the π-noise learned by SimCLR(Chen et al., 2020) with PiNDA on STL-10. We aim to learn the π-noise with a Gaussian distribution N(µ, Σ). We fix µ as 0 and only learn the variance of Gaussian π-noise, which is visualized in the second row. The third row is a sampling noise and the fourth row contains the images added with π-noise. Compared with other visualizations, the noise is first normalized and then fed into the contrastive module. From the visualization, we find that the π- noise generator successfully learns effective visual augmentations (like style transfer) with only original images.
abstract: Inspired by the idea of Positive-incentive Noise (Pi-Noise or $Ï$-Noise) that aims at learning the reliable noise beneficial to tasks, we scientifically investigate the connection between contrastive learning and $Ï$-noise in this paper. By converting the contrastive loss to an auxiliary Gaussian distribution to quantitatively measure the difficulty of the specific contrastive model under the information theory framework, we properly define the task entropy, the core concept of $Ï$-noise, of contrastive learning. It is further proved that the predefined data augmentation in the standard contrastive learning paradigm can be regarded as a kind of point estimation of $Ï$-noise. Inspired by the theoretical study, a framework that develops a $Ï$-noise generator to learn the beneficial noise (instead of estimation) as data augmentations for contrast is proposed. The designed framework can be applied to diverse types of data and is also completely compatible with the existing contrastive models. From the visualization, we surprisingly find that the proposed method successfully learns effective augmentations. Our code is available at https://github.com/hyzhang98/PiNDA.
